atomic.decision: The package singleton, version and standard severity metadata remain public and coherent.
Registration, thresholding, formatting and removal preserve independent handler identity.
A custom named level keeps its number, icon and threshold behavior distinct from numeric calls.
A bound view adds captured context without contaminating the original logger.
Nested contextual values shadow, extend and restore the prior mapping.
Configured and view-local patchers share one record in documented order.
Independent callable filters route contextual records without cross-sink leakage.
Serialized output preserves rendered text and structured record fields as one JSON line.
Prepared sink routes stay invisible until atomically committed and reopen with stable identity.
Route revisions are idempotent, parent-complete, acyclic and conflict rejecting.
A delivery lease owns one canonical route closure, owner and generation.
Lease handoff preserves selection while fencing the stale owner.
Dispatch attempts separate prepared, terminal and acknowledged visibility.
Sink artifacts publish exact bytes atomically and verify their content identity.
Entered delivery resources create durable reverse-order drain obligations.
Delivery events separate prepare, publish, claim and acknowledgement.

composition.decision: Level and contextual selection compose across two sinks without leakage.
Caught sink failure preserves a healthy sibling while uncaught failure reaches the caller.
A standard logging handler receives severity, rendered message and structured extra together.
Completion awaits multiple accepted coroutine deliveries with their bound context.
Only the latest committed sink-route revision is eligible for a fresh delivery lease.
A rejected route replacement preserves the last dispatchable revision and receipt lineage.
Reopened route and artifact stores retain one revision identity.
Overlapping route selections deduplicate a dependency-first closure without unrelated carryover.
A stale lease owner cannot continue a dispatch attempt after transfer.
Lease handoff transfers event ownership while preserving route-local order.
Only work admitted by the current delivery lease creates a journal attempt.
Dispatch failure publishes no success while retaining all drain obligations.
Completed-unacknowledged recovery verifies exact sink bytes before one acknowledgement.
A failed dispatch emits terminal failure information and never becomes successful current state.
A sink rendition binds the route revision that produced it.
Interrupted artifact preparation is invisible and resumes atomically for the same dispatch.
A changed route advances one artifact generation while a sibling remains verified.
Artifact corruption fails closed before a successful delivery event becomes visible.
Drain frames are admitted only for the current fenced delivery lease.
Entered sink resources unwind in reverse after a journaled dispatch failure.
Artifact replacement waits for owed drain work and rollback preserves prior bytes.
An acknowledged dispatch creates one ordered event batch whose interrupted delivery stays pending.
A stale event claimant cannot acknowledge delivery after ownership changes.
Event order reflects resource entry and discharge across reopen without duplicate acknowledgement.
One application workflow separates console and file thresholds while retaining bound context in durable file output.
Concurrent contexts remain isolated across two complete per-thread emission sequences.
One successful relay closes route, lease, dispatch, exact bytes, drain and event receipts.
Relay failure preserves the previous acknowledged generation and a corrected retry publishes once.
Ownership transfer fences stale work and a reopened coordinator resumes one receipt closure.
Overlapping sink selection converges while an independent failure cannot pollute the winner.
A crash between completion and acknowledgement recovers exactly once without duplicate sink publication or event.
Corrupt or cyclic receipt closure fails closed and leaves the last acknowledged delivery visible.
